question: The atomic number of an element is the number of_______ in the nucleus of each atom of that element.
solution:
The correct answer is__** protons**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **number of protons** in the nucleus of an atom of a given element is **called the atomic number of that element.**
 
• This number uniquely identifies the element and determines its position in the periodic table.
 
• For example, **hydrogen has an atomic number of 1 (one proton), while carbon has an atomic number of 6 (six protons)**
 
• The **atomic number also indicates the number of electrons in a neutral atom o**f the element, balancing the positive charge of the protons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neutrons**

 
 
• **​**Neutrons are subatomic particles found in the nucleus of an atom, alongside protons.
 
• They have no electrical charge (neutral) and are slightly more massive than protons.
 
• Neutrons contribute to the mass of the atom and play a crucial role in stabilizing the nucleus
 
• Neutrons are essential in nuclear reactions, such as fission and fusion. 
 
 
 
• **Electrons**
 
 
• **​**Electrons are negatively charged subatomic particles that orbit the nucleus of an atom in electron shells or energy levels.
 
• They are much less massive than protons and neutrons.
 
• The number and arrangement of electrons determine an element's chemical properties and behavior. 
 
• Electrons are responsible for electrical conductivity. 
 
 
 
• **Mesons**
 
 
• **​**Mesons are a type of subatomic particle composed of a quark and an antiquark.
 
• They are part of the family of particles known as hadrons, which also include baryons (like protons and neutrons).
 
• Mesons mediate the strong nuclear force that holds protons and neutrons together in the nucleus
 
• There are several types of mesons, including pions (π mesons) and kaons (K mesons).
